correctness.rationale: For the specified cumulative projector, multiply E_i+z(I−E_i) and retain coefficients through k. On a face using j atomless-coordinate point masses, the factor is z^j(1−z)^(m−j) times the Boolean product of 1+zZ_i. The mutually singular face measures give the stated variation upper bound. For sharpness use an exceptional interval of mass ε and evaluate on the atom where all m indicators are exceptional and each sign is fixed. Including actual probabilities in the row, j matches contribute the factor [ε(1−z)+z]^j[(1−ε)(1−z)]^(m−j), which converges coefficientwise to the atomless face factor; the finite absolute row sum therefore approaches the bound. A row sign choice realizes the norm on an atom of positive measure, and integral pairing gives the L1 equality, so pointwise representatives cause no gap. In the window, the first two formal log coefficients of the scaled Boolean product are the normalized sign sum and −1/2, and the higher fixed coefficients vanish. The atomless factor adds drift −λ, giving He_(k−j)(G−λ)/(k−j)! for its top normalized coefficient. E e_l^2=binom(n,l) supplies uniform integrability, and the binomial multiplicities converge as stated. For m≫√n and fixed k the l>0 terms vanish at scale m^(k−j) in L1, and the l=0 alternating binomial sum gives the coefficient (−1)^(k−j)/(k−j)!. The leading Hermite monomial gives the independent high-λ limit. The argument covers k=0 for the finite formula and the pure-coordinate cases; at k=2 the Boolean constant is 2φ(1)=sqrt(2/(πe)). It establishes the norm of this projector, not least norm among all projections on the atomless product. The finite checker was inspected but not executed.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct result is the fixed-k joint asymptotic, in particular the finite nonzero λ shifted-Hermite window for mixed atomless and Boolean coordinates, together with its diffuse-dominated comparison. The Boolean endpoint is established in the literature. For most stated finite parameters the exact mixed constant is already implied by a same-day finite-alphabet theorem plus the standard dyadic approximation, so this aspect is not credited as separately new.
residual_risks: The original's reference to a published Bernoulli rare-vertex theorem is not pinned to a source; the described first-chaos mechanism does not itself give the mixed shift, but this overlap is not exhaustively resolved.
A more general triangular-array kernel theorem might yield part of the asymptotic; no inspected work gives the shifted mixed profile. Same-day catalogue dates do not establish priority.

value.rationale: Cumulative low-interaction approximations on products can amplify sup and mean absolute error. The mixed theorem identifies exactly when adding a minority of atomless inputs changes the leading stability constant and gives an explicit interpolation across that window. The shifted-Hermite variation sum is more informative than separate growth estimates in the pure-coordinate models.
